ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, there is a single-transistor common-emitter amplifier circuit. The input signal Ui is applied to the base of transistor VT through coupling capacitor C1; the base is connected to +VCC and ground by upper and lower bias resistors. The collector is connected to +VCC through Rc, and from the collector node it is connected through output coupling capacitor C2 to the load RL on the right side, with output Uo taken across RL. The emitter is connected to ground through Re, and bypass capacitor Ce is connected in parallel to ground. Then reason: When finding the output resistance Ro, process according to the small-signal AC equivalent: remove the load RL and set the input signal to zero; C1, C2, and Ce are regarded as short circuits in the midband AC equivalent; the DC power supply VCC is taken as AC ground. Since the input is set to zero and C1 is short-circuited, the base is at AC ground; the short circuit of Ce makes the emitter at AC ground, so vbe=0, and the controlled source does not provide an independent output path. The transistor output resistance ro is not given in the problem, so it is treated as infinite. The output end is equivalent to the collector node through the C2 short circuit, so looking into the output end, only Rc connected to AC ground is seen. Given Rc=10 kΩ, therefore Ro=10 kΩ.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as a common-emitter amplifier with output coupled by C2 from the collector node to RL. To find Ro, remove RL, set the input signal to zero, short C1/C2/Ce for the AC equivalent, and ground VCC. The base and emitter become AC-grounded, so the controlled source contributes no independent output path; with r_o not specified, treat it as infinite. The output test source applied at the C2/output terminal therefore sees the collector resistor Rc directly to AC ground. Substitute the text value Rc = 10 kΩ, giving Ro = 10 kΩ.
